xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-2542: add GPT-5.6 (Sol/Terra/Luna) family, make gpt-5.6-sol the new OpenAI default

plan.title: feat(models): add GPT-5.6 (Sol/Terra/Luna) family, make gpt-5.6-sol the new OpenAI default
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-4-8

narratives.Problem: OpenAI released the GPT-5.6 family on 2026-07-09 in three tiers — Sol (flagship), Terra (balanced), Luna (fast/cheap) — and names gpt-5.6-sol as its own recommended Codex default. Overdeck's model registry only knows the gpt-5.5 generation, so these models cannot be selected, priced, gated, or defaulted to.
narratives.Proposal: Execute the pre-verified PRD at .pan/drafts/pan-2542.md verbatim. Register all three tiers everywhere gpt-5.5 is registered (type union, provider/router/fallback maps, capability matrix, pricing, subscription gating, dashboard pickers/catalog, MODEL_API_IDS), add automated tests locking in their context ceiling / subscription gating / list presence / cost parsing, and repoint exactly three defaults from gpt-5.5 to gpt-5.6-sol (providers.ts opus tier + the two dashboard picker preferred-model defaults). Every pricing/context/skill figure is dictated by the PRD's verified-reference table or its mechanical derivation rules — nothing is invented. The work is decomposed into 15 mostly-parallel beads over a small typing foundation.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Do not modify gpt-5.5, gpt-5.5-pro, or any gpt-5.4* entry VALUES; the only non-additive edits are the three explicit default pointers (providers.ts tierModels.opus, chat ModelPicker HARNESS_DEFAULT_MODEL.ohmypi, shared ModelPicker 'preferred' default).
- Do not deprecate or remove gpt-5.5.
- Do not 'fix' the pre-existing stale `$3/$18` comment on the gpt-5.5 capability entry (model-capabilities.ts:489) — it is out-of-scope pre-existing drift.
- Do not change the sonnet/haiku tier pointers in providers.ts.
- Do not invent a SWE-bench Verified score for any gpt-5.6 tier — none was published at launch; write 'not published at launch' in doc SWE-bench columns.
- Do not run `pan sync` to regenerate the rendered ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — that is a post-merge machine-level operator step, not an acceptance criterion.
- Do not execute skills/okf/scripts/selftest.sh — it makes real billed Codex CLI calls; static text edit only.
- Do not touch reference/token-spend-report.mdx, docs/ROLES.md:95, src/lib/agents/__tests__/staffing.test.ts, .../tier-table.test.ts, .pan/records, .pan/continues, .beads/issues.jsonl, docs/design/*.html, or .release/*.md — verified out of scope during planning.

autoDecisions.summary: Execute the PRD verbatim with no clarifying questions.
autoDecisions.rationale: The PRD is a fully-specified, pre-verified implementation brief: exact file paths, line numbers, before/after snippets, verified external reference data, FRs, ACs, and explicit out-of-scope notes for all 14 work items. It leaves no open decision for the operator to make.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep all Work-Item-14 doc/prompt updates as ONE bead rather than splitting per-file.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every edit is the same logical change (reflect the new family + new default in prose) and each is mechanically identical; splitting ~8 trivial wording edits into separate beads adds tracking overhead with no reviewability benefit. Decomposition guidance treats a coherent doc cluster as one bead.

Each bead is a mechanical additive edit dictated verbatim by a PRD before/after snippet. A reviewer verifies correctness against the PRD from a small diff, and any wrong model-ID string surfaces immediately at typecheck. The work.inspect gate would rubber-stamp mechanical diffs, not catch judgment defects — its intended value does not apply here.

autoDecisions.summary: Split PRD Work Item 10 (two dashboard pickers) into two per-file beads.
autoDecisions.rationale: The chat ModelPicker.tsx and shared ModelPicker/ModelPicker.tsx are distinct files, each independently reviewable; per the one-file-one-bead heuristic they are cleaner as two beads. Both still trace FR-5, and D2 records that these two defaults plus providers.ts are the only non-additive edits.
